title: S3 Versioning & Replication
summary: Copy objects across Regions or accounts, with predictable timing and multi-Region endpoints.
tldr: S3 Replication copies new objects asynchronously to another bucket: **CRR** across Regions, **SRR** in the same Region. **Versioning must be on in both buckets.**
Need a guaranteed time? Turn on **S3 Replication Time Control (RTC)**: designed for 99.99% of new objects in 15 minutes, backed by an SLA, with metrics and missed-threshold events.
Replication only applies to objects written *after* the rule exists. Existing or **FAILED** objects need **S3 Batch Replication**.
**Multi-Region Access Points** give one global endpoint over buckets in several Regions, with active-passive failover controls.

keyFacts.text: **RTC** is designed to replicate 99.99% of new objects within 15 minutes (the SLA commits to 99.9%), and emits events when an object misses the threshold.
Required on source and destination. Once enabled, versioning can only be *suspended*, never turned off. Delete markers replicate only if you enable it.
Objects encrypted with KMS replicate only if the rule opts in and names a destination key; the replication role needs `kms:Decrypt` on source and `kms:Encrypt` on destination.
For active-active buckets, create rules in both directions and turn on **replica modification sync** so metadata changes flow back.
**EFS replication** keeps a read-only copy in another Region or AZ with a 15-minute RPO for most file systems. Delete the replication to make it writable.

traps: Deleting and recreating a replication rule does **not** replicate old objects. Use Batch Replication.
Transfer Acceleration speeds client uploads over the internet. It has nothing to do with replication time.
S3 Replication without RTC has no time SLA, so it can't satisfy "within 15 minutes, backed by an SLA".
SRR keeps the copy in the same Region, which doesn't protect against a Regional outage.
Suspending versioning doesn't delete existing noncurrent versions; use Lifecycle rules to expire them.
Lifecycle actions are not replicated, and replication doesn't make a destination immutable. Add Object Lock (compliance mode) if deletions must be blocked.
Route 53 CNAMEs pointing to bucket REST endpoints don't work as failover. Use a Multi-Region Access Point or a CloudFront origin group.
